<!-- pr-reviewer: b20b3d30bafb79cd2b25c2c6acabc21fa0ee0621 -->
Needs changes before merge.

The wire tool supplies the diameter to the path and the operation stamp. The machine condition supplies the spark gap. The new checks reject incompatible wire diameters and excessive spark gaps.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/app/src/project/validate.rs:205`: Keep existing wire projects readable. Before this change, a Wire Contour had to store an empty `tool` string. This check rejects that valid saved state as corrupt. No load migration supplies a wire tool. A local probe reconstructed the previous file layout, with an empty wire tool reference and no wire tool entity. The load returned `Err(Corrupt("'Legacy' names no tool"))`. Add a load migration or a safe recovery state. Add a test that opens a file saved before this change. Preserve its wire diameter and prevent posting until the tool state is valid.
2. `crates/app/tests/wire_verify_tol.rs:157`: Update the current-main fixture for the new tool requirement. Both tests create `Punch1` with an empty tool name. Both fail with `op: NotFound("")` after the trial merge. Add and mount a valid wire tool in this fixture. Keep the existing tolerance, posting, and project assertions.
3. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs:212` and the PR body: Add before/after screenshots for the UI changes. The body has no screenshots. Show the wire tool controls and the affected catalog/type choices. Store the images only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch, and link them from the body.

Local checks used a clean trial merge with upstream main `57f2ffbbf51a32e9f71be6d4d0014184b1713f41`. No GitHub runner was used.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-tools --lib` | 85 passed |
| App `mcp_wire_contour` | 5 passed |
| App `sodick_alc400g`, `sodick_wire_post` | 5 and 9 passed |
| App `tool_gate`, `tool_law` | 9 and 4 passed |
| App `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_fans` | 8, 3, 8, and 2 passed |
| App `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_tabs` | 12, 7, 7, and 4 passed |
| App `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_tool`, `wire_verify` | 7, 5, 4, and 3 passed |
| App `wire_verify_tol` | 2 failed; see item 2 |
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --lib`, from `crates/ui` | Build failed; no UI tests ran |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |
| Same clippy check with `-p camcraft-ui` | Build failed |

The UI build and clippy failure is also present in the source on current upstream main. `short_caption` lacks the `Waterjet` arm. This PR does not change that match. This is a separate upstream limitation:

```text
error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `camcraft_app::machine::Kind::Waterjet` not covered
  --> crates/ui/src/machine_modes.rs:44:11
```

I ran two of the stated mutations independently:

- Bypass `wire::refusal` for a Wire tool: the command test failed on the missing `rpm must be 0` diagnostic. The generic tool check still rejected the bad RPM.
- Disable the `gap >= wire_diameter * 0.5` guard: the mismatch test failed because the excessive gap was accepted.

After I restored both files, all four `wire_tool` tests passed. I also removed the temporary load probe. No review changes remain in the source tree.

No NC or CL golden file changes. I checked the changed `ONE_PROFILE_STAMP` constant and its fixture line by line. The fixture now mounts `EDM-W025`, and the stamp includes the tool digest before the condition digest.

The full quick gate, release gate, pixel snapshots, and physical machine tests were not run. UI verification remains blocked by the upstream build error.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:
1. Legacy wire projects now open in a safe recovery state. The saved machine condition and wire diameter are preserved. Cached paths and stamps are cleared. Posting requires an explicitly assigned valid wire tool. Pinned by wire_tool::legacy_wire_project_opens_without_a_tool_and_requires_recovery_before_posting. Validation, recovery, stamp, and cache mutations each went RED, then GREEN after restoration.
2. The wire_verify_tol fixture now mounts EDM-W025. Both existing tests pass with their tolerance, posting, and project assertions retained. Restoring the empty tool makes both tests RED; restoring the fixture makes both GREEN.
3. The PR body links eight actual before/after screenshots for catalog entries, catalog types, New Tool types, and tool controls. Images live only on the fork's pr-screenshots branch. All links return valid PNGs. The edm_tool_visibility tests pass; bypassing either catalog or New Tool filtering makes them RED, and restoring the filters makes them GREEN.

New head: 4a9c638436bbd3e6f4a86907f4c3a4a8e7a27c4c.
Upstream main was merged cleanly. The quick gate passed tools and all 281 app binaries. The gate and clippy including UI are RED on the existing upstream short_caption Waterjet match error (E0004). Tools/app clippy passes with -D warnings. No unrelated UI fix was added.

Please re-review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4a9c638436bbd3e6f4a86907f4c3a4a8e7a27c4c -->
Needs changes before merge.

The three findings from the previous review are addressed. Legacy wire projects open in a safe recovery state. The load clears their cached paths and generation stamps. The machine conditions remain unchanged. Generation and posting require an explicitly assigned wire tool. The recovery test passes. Both `wire_verify_tol` tests pass with the mounted wire tool. The PR body links eight valid before/after PNG images on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/edm_tool_visibility.rs:101`: Use a fixed mode table without `SinkerEdm` for the negative case. Current upstream main includes `SinkerEdm` in `MACHINE_MODES`. Thus `tool_kind_offered_for` correctly returns true, and this new assertion fails. Use the fixed table for the mounted-only positive case too. Keep a separate positive case with selectable `SinkerEdm`. The test must pass with current main and still test each visibility rule.

Local checks used a clean trial merge with upstream main `a49322b9c0c049bd0b3b2d1dea855de6087ac64b`. No GitHub runner was used. Current main fixes the earlier Waterjet build error.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-tools --lib` | 85 passed |
| App `mcp_wire_contour` | 5 passed |
| App `sodick_alc400g`, `sodick_wire_post` | 5 and 9 passed |
| App `tool_gate`, `tool_law` | 9 and 4 passed |
| App `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_fans` | 8, 3, 8, and 2 passed |
| App `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_tabs` | 12, 7, 7, and 4 passed |
| App `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_tool`, `wire_verify`, `wire_verify_tol` | 7, 5, 5, 3, and 2 passed |
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --lib`, from `crates/ui` | Built; 915 passed, 1 failed, 6 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` | Plan read; full gate not run |

The UI failure is:

```text
thread 'egui_app::tests::edm_tool_visibility::sinker_electrode_is_offered_only_when_sinker_edm_is_selectable_or_mounted' panicked at crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/edm_tool_visibility.rs:101:5:
assertion failed: !crate::machine_modes::tool_kind_offered_for(ToolKind::Electrode,
        &crate::machine_modes::MACHINE_MODES, &[MachineKind::Mill])
```

This is a safety-tier review. I repeated two stated mutations independently:

- Disable the `gap >= wire_diameter * 0.5` guard: the mismatch test failed at `gap 0.10 >= radius 0.08`.
- Retain the legacy generation stamp: the recovery test failed at `legacy generation stamp is discarded`.

After each restoration, all five `wire_tool` tests passed. No review changes remain in the source tree.

No NC or CL golden files changed. I checked the changed `ONE_PROFILE_STAMP` constant and its fixture line by line. The fixture mounts `EDM-W025`. The stamp includes the mounted tool digest before the machine condition digest.

The full quick gate, release gate, pixel snapshots, and physical machine tests were not run. The PR merges cleanly, but the UI test failure requires `needs-rework`. The draft stays a draft.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:
1. The Sinker visibility test now uses a fixed milling-only mode table for the negative and mounted-only cases. The separate selectable-Sinker positive case remains. Pinned by `sinker_electrode_is_offered_only_when_sinker_edm_is_selectable_or_mounted`. Reverting this fix makes the test RED; restoring it makes it GREEN. Disabling either visibility rule independently also makes it RED, then GREEN after restoration.

The pin and mutation runs used a temporary Waterjet match arm to unblock this branch's existing UI compile error. That arm was removed afterward and is not committed.

New head: 9c0c0ae9111df2f975b09ae6aa667044a87653e1.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is RED on the unchanged `short_caption` missing Waterjet arm (E0004). Tools and all 281 selected app test binaries passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is RED on the same compile error. The commit changes only the requested test. The PR remains a draft.

Please re-review.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

All previous findings are addressed. The Sinker visibility test uses a fixed milling-only table for the negative and mounted-only cases. A separate positive case includes selectable Sinker EDM. Both visibility tests pass with current main.

Legacy Wire Contour projects open in a recovery state. The load clears their cached paths and generation stamps. The machine conditions remain unchanged. Generation and posting require an explicitly assigned wire tool. The recovery test and both `wire_verify_tol` tests pass.

The PR body links eight valid before/after PNG images on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. I inspected the tool controls and catalog menu images. They show the wire controls and the changed tool choices. The PR does not change release snapshot PNGs.

Local checks used a clean trial merge with upstream main `dab6498aed0ab078a97f0892c417d161135219fa`. I used no GitHub runner. I checked the laws in the current upstream `AGENTS.md`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | Passed |
| Tools library tests | 85 passed |
| App `mcp_wire_contour`, `sodick_alc400g`, `sodick_wire_post` | 5, 5, and 9 passed |
| App `tool_gate`, `tool_law` | 9 and 4 passed |
| App `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_fans` | 8, 3, 8, and 2 passed |
| App `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_tabs` | 12, 7, 7, and 4 passed |
| App `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_tool`, `wire_verify`, `wire_verify_tol` | 7, 5, 5, 3, and 2 passed |
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --lib`, from `crates/ui` | 916 passed, 6 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` | Plan read; full gate not run |

This is a safety-tier review. I repeated two stated mutations independently:

- Disable the `gap >= wire_diameter * 0.5` guard: the mismatch test failed at `gap 0.10 >= radius 0.08`.
- Retain the legacy path cache: the recovery test failed at `legacy cache cannot authorize posting`.

After each restoration, all five `wire_tool` tests passed. No review edits remain in the source files.

No NC or CL golden files changed. I checked the changed `ONE_PROFILE_STAMP` constant and its fixture line by line. The fixture mounts `EDM-W025`. The stamp includes the mounted tool digest before the machine condition digest.

Requested before merge: none.

Non-blocking note: `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs:96` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs:73` add code to files near or above 400 lines. Consider a later split along the condition-validation and tool-kind selection boundaries.

The full quick gate, release gate, ignored pixel tests, and physical machine tests were not run. The local build, selected tests, and clippy passed. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
